item.description:

item.title: Guia de GSM de papel de seda para embalagem
item.description:
GSM é o peso de um metro quadrado de papel. Mais GSM costuma dar mais opacidade e corpo—não automaticamente “mais premium”.

GSM (grams per square meter) is the weight of one square meter of paper. For tissue, higher GSM usually means more opacity and a sturdier wrap—not automatically “more premium.”

Why GSM matters in unboxing

Tissue does three jobs at once:

  1. Protect the product
  2. Carry brand color / pattern
  3. Create the first tactile moment when the box opens

Wrong GSM shows up as see-through logos, tearing at folds, or a limp wrap that feels cheap next to a premium product.

item.title: Comparação de materiais para hang tags
item.description:
O hang tag é pequeno, mas carrega preço, tamanho e marca no momento da decisão. O suporte deve combinar com o produto e a fixação.

Hang tags are small, but they carry price, size, origin, and brand voice at the exact moment a shopper decides. Material choice should match fabric hand-feel, print detail, and how the tag will be attached.

What hang tags must survive

  • Sewing / tagging line handling
  • Steam, light moisture, or warehouse dust
  • Customer trying the garment on
  • Photography for PDP (product detail page)

If the tag curls, bleeds, or frays after one try-on, it undermines the product.

item.title: Checklist proof-to-bulk de embalagem
item.description:
A maioria das falhas é de processo: bulk sem assinatura de amostra, ou ficheiro alterado após aprovação.

Most packaging failures are process failures: bulk starts before anyone signed the real sample, or a “final” file quietly changed after approval. Use this checklist on every new SKU and every major reorder.

Stage A — Brief (before anyone quotes tooling)

Confirm in writing:

  • Product line(s): stickers / tags / tissue / bags / boxes / finishes
  • Sizes and quantities (bands OK)
  • Brand colors (Pantone preferred for logos)
  • Substrate and finish intent
  • Ship-to region and timing window

If tooling (dies, foil stamps) is needed, it should be explicit in the quote—not a surprise invoice later.
